# ASP11 Practice Item Bank — sample for tests (rows copied from the real bank)

## Batch D1-01 (D1-0001 to D1-0025)

| ID | Domain-Task | Level | Stem | A | B | C | D | Key | Rationale | Reference | Est. Diff. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1-0001 | D1-T1 | Application | A horizontal cylindrical diesel tank has an inside diameter of 10 ft and a length of 12 ft. Using 7.48 gal/ft³, what is the full capacity of the tank? | 126 gal | 942 gal | 1,410 gal | 7,050 gal | D | V = πr²L = 3.1416 × 5² × 12 = 942.5 ft³; 942.5 × 7.48 = 7,050 gal. A: divides by 7.48 instead of multiplying. B: stops at ft³ with no gallon conversion. C: uses r instead of r² (π × 5 × 12 × 7.48). | Yates, 4th ed., Ch. 5 Math Review, Common Geometric Equations, p. 220; Ch. 18 Water Properties, p. 469 | 70 |
| D1-0023 | D1-T14 | Analysis | Air sampling shows a worker exposed to three solvents with additive effects: Solvent X 40 ppm (TLV 100 ppm), Solvent Y 90 ppm (TLV 300 ppm), and Solvent Z 250 ppm (TLV 500 ppm). Which conclusion about the mixture exposure is correct? | Exceeded; the summed C/TLV ratio is 1.20 | Acceptable; the highest single ratio is 0.50 | Acceptable; pooled concentration over pooled TLV is 0.42 | Acceptable; the mean of the three ratios is 0.40 | A | For additive effects, sum each C/TLV: 0.40 + 0.30 + 0.50 = 1.20 > 1, so the mixture limit is exceeded even though each solvent is individually below its TLV. B: judges compliance by one component only. C: pools concentrations (380/900), which has no basis. D: averages ratios instead of summing them. | Yates, 4th ed., Ch. 6, Gaseous Mixtures, p. 243 | 55 |

**Coverage log**

## Batch D2-01 (D2-0001 to D2-0025)

| ID | Domain-Task | Level | Stem | A | B | C | D | Key | Rationale | Reference | Est. Diff. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D2-0005 | D2-T2 | Application | A fabrication shop replaces its solvent-based coating with a water-based coating to reduce painters' exposure to volatile organic compounds. Which level of the hierarchy of controls does this change represent? | Elimination | Substitution | Engineering control | Administrative control | B | Replacing a more hazardous material with a less hazardous one is substitution; a water-based paint in place of a solvent-based paint is the reference's example. A: elimination removes the hazard entirely; painting still occurs with a different material. C: engineering controls modify equipment or the workspace (e.g., spray booth ventilation). D: administrative controls change how or when people work. | Yates, 4th ed., Ch. 35 Prevention through Design, ANSI Hierarchy of Controls (Substitution), p. 790 | 80 |
| D2-0018 | D2-T8a | Application | A crew is laying pipe in a 5-ft-deep, 120-ft-long trench. What is the maximum lateral travel distance permitted from any worker in the trench to a means of egress? | 10 ft | 25 ft | 35 ft | 50 ft | B | Trenches 4 ft or more deep must have a safe means of egress, such as a ladder, within 25 ft of lateral travel. A: is more restrictive than required. C and D: exceed the 25-ft limit. | Yates, 4th ed., Ch. 25 Construction Safety, Safe Entry and Exit, p. 571 | 75 |
| D2-0011 | D2-T3 | Application | A supervisor is beginning a job hazard analysis of a drum-filling task. What is the recommended way to break the job down into steps? | Observe a worker doing the job and record each step as it occurs | Copy the steps from the equipment manufacturer's manual | Record every hand and eye motion so that no detail is missed | Have the area supervisor describe the steps from memory | A | Watching the employee perform the job and listing each step as it is taken, then reviewing the steps with the employee, captures the job as actually performed. B: a manual may not reflect how the job is actually done. C: an overly detailed breakdown becomes unnecessarily long. D: recall from memory misses steps and excludes the worker. | OSHA 3071, Job Hazard Analysis, Step 5: Outline the steps or tasks, p. 5 | 78 |

## Batch D9-01 (D9-0001 to D9-0025)

| ID | Domain-Task | Level | Stem | A | B | C | D | Key | Rationale | Reference | Est. Diff. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D9-0025 | D9-T4 | Application | A worker's recordable occupational illness is a diagnosed mental illness. How must the worker's name be handled on the OSHA 300 Log? | Enter only the worker's initials and job title | Enter the full name as for any other case | Leave the case off the log entirely | Enter "privacy case" in place of the name | D | Mental illnesses are privacy cases, so "privacy case" is entered in place of the employee's name. A: initials can identify the worker and are not the prescribed entry. B: discloses the worker's identity. C: the case is still recordable. | Yates, 4th ed., Ch. 3 Reporting Occupational Injuries and Illnesses, How Are Privacy Cases Listed on the Forms?, p. 50 | 80 |
